newsitem.title: USA: World Bank approves $500 mln loans to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves $500 mln loans to Argentina.

text.p: The World Bank said it approved two loans totalling $500 million to the Argentine government to help with pension reform and a flood protection programme.
The bank said it was lending $300 million over 15 years to help the Argentine government bring mainly provincial civil servants into its new pension system, which it began privatising in 1994.
The Inter-American Development Bank will provide a further $320 million to the project, with the remaining $706 million to be financed by the government, the World Bank said in a statement.

The bank also said it was contributing a $200 million loan to a $488 million project aimed at protecting the economic assets of people living in the flood-prone Parana River basin. The Japanese Export-Import Bank would provide a further $120 million.
The bank did not disclose the terms of the loans.
